settings.heading: The advice is consistent. So is the outcome.

settings.content: Read enough first-hand accounts and the same sentences repeat — from friends, forums, clinics.

settings.lines:
“It might resolve when you wean.”
“Unfortunately, you’ll just have to wait it out.”
“She said she couldn’t do anything until I’m done breastfeeding.”

settings.content: So you wait. Then, months later, a second set follows — just as consistent.

settings.lines:
“My worst flare was when I stopped breastfeeding.”
“Seven months postpartum, and it came back the worst it’s ever been.”

settings.content: Both sets are the same women, at different points.
Which leaves the question the advice skips. Why would skin get worse just as the hormones settle?
